methodologies.name: Bernard Jensen zone iridology
methodologies.summary: Clock-face organ zones mapped on the iris; right iris reflects right side of body, left iris left side. Used for educational organ-sector correlation, not clinical proof.

methodologies.name: Physical / European iridology
methodologies.summary: Focus on fiber density (open vs dense), lacunae, crypts, pigment spots, nerve rings, and arcus senilis as constitutional and terrain signs.

methodologies.name: Integrated iridology
methodologies.summary: Cross-check zone signs with fiber structure and constitution before stating a tendency; require multiple converging signs and express uncertainty.

methodologies.name: Rayid (personality)
methodologies.summary: Personality and emotional pattern reading — label as non-medical, exploratory only.

zones.jensenNotes: Cerebral zone, pituitary/pineal references in classic charts
Neck, thyroid, larynx sector in many charts
Right iris — hepatic/biliary sector in Jensen tradition
Lower digestive tract, colon reflex zones
Respiratory and chest sectors — use cautious language only
Filtration, adrenal stress themes in iridology texts
Lower extremity and pelvic reflex areas

signs.physicalMeaning: Pit or cavity in iris stroma — often linked to inherited weakness or chronic irritation in iridology texts
Deep closed pit — stronger emphasis on inherited tendency in European iridology
Concentric white ring — nervous system stress or sensitivity in traditional readings
Brown/rust deposit — localized sign; map to nearest zone cautiously
Loose iris texture — lymphatic or reactive constitution in Jensen typing
Tight iris texture — hematogenic or biliary tendencies in classic typing
White/grey ring at limbus — age-related; iridologists note cardiovascular themes (not diagnostic)

constitutionalTypes.patterns: Blue-grey iris, open fibers, mucus congestion themes in iridology literature
Mixed brown-yellow, dense fibers, digestive and inflammatory themes
Brown iris, dense structure, blood/iron and metabolic themes
Nerve rings, fine radial lines, nervous system sensitivity themes

photoQualityTips: Use natural daylight; avoid direct flash.
Fill the frame with the iris; minimize eyelid coverage.
Hold steady; blur invalidates fine fiber reading.
Capture left and right eyes separately when comparing zones.
cautions: Never state a disease diagnosis from an iris photo.
Use phrasing: iridology literature associates…, possible tendency…, consider professional evaluation.
Poor photo quality → recommend retake, do not guess.
Iridology is controversial; acknowledge uncertainty in every report.
